convoLines.text: "I asked Dieter about this wound — Dieter's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"a ridge with a view for miles — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Dieter is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"I rinse the cup twice. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Mateo grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Mateo is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
Ruth seems lighter — something good landed recently.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Dieter owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Sleep's gone strange. I check everyone's shoes for wear at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Mateo nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Goldenrod — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
«¡Hola! ¿Cómo te llamas?»
They answer at length. They nod back, slowly.
They answer at length. They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed. "No, no." — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
They answer at length. You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
Give me something to do. Anything. I can't stand sitting here wondering if I'm dead weight.
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
"All right —" Mateo starts to stand, then sinks back down. "Maybe not today. The fire's got me."
"It's not about them believing in me. It's about me believing it first."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on wanting to prove they're useful."
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "I dreamed Dieter was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ruth nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
You show them Goldenrod — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Ruth shifts their weight. "I need something to do. Anything. Please."
Their whole posture softens around you.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Since Dieter died... I keep expecting to see Dieter at the fire. Stupid."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
Mateo nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I can't reach this properly. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"This one — Pawpaw. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Lucas is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Hannah has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Sleep's gone strange. I wake before anyone else at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ruth nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Nobody says Lucas's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.
A gesture, patient and clear: palms up, then toward you.
"Yeah? What's up? Gotta keep moving."
They answer at length. They nod, holding your gaze a beat longer.
They answer at length. A grin breaks through, quick and warm. "Water?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
They answer at length. You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it.
They glance toward their own thoughts; the exchange is winding down.
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Dieter Grabowski is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Dieter Grabowski is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Dieter kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Dieter's gone." Mateo looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Dieter." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Elijah blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Tainted Bait (Level 1). Your bait is tainted — traps catch 50% more. (The poison’s in the bait, not your hands. Mostly.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Wire Snares (Level 1). A loop of wire on a game trail. Simple, effective, ancient. Check at dawn.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Tripwire (Level 1). You string a wire at ankle height. The next monster that moves eats dirt — prone, stunned, and embarrassed. (Sets up the party.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading People (Level 1). Microexpressions leak truth. Watch the eyes, not the mouth. People tell you who they are.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Deep Read! You don't just read trust — you read intent. Know what they'll do next. (Your knowledge of Reading People amplifies your open_book.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Field Dressing (Level 1). Break down game fast and clean. Less waste, more meat, usable parts.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Dieter Grabowski, 41 days. The mantle passes to Elijah Justice.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Elijah Justice, 44 — an exterminator. Their hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Echo Location, Dowsing.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Dieter — and Dieter is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Mateo, Ruth speak for Elijah — "Dieter trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Elijah before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.

lastSay: d57: 💀 Naran starved. Slowly. Nobody eats much tonight. The pot stays full and nobody touches it.
d57: ⚠ Haven's pantry is empty. Day 3 of hunger.
d57: Haven couldn't hold. On the third hungry day, people started walking — in different directions. The scattering, again.
d57: 🌿 Lemongrass — the foragers have handled it 8 days running. They know it now — which parts are worth hauling, which bruise, how it wants to be carried. The village's knowledge deepens.
d57: 💡 Lemongrass: the village knows more than you do. Harvest it a few more times (0/3) and it'll click.
